knowledge_gaps: Reproducibility requires explicit prefix/target selection, repeated-item handling, padding and truncation rules, scoring tensor shapes, candidate counts, and tie-breaking. Training-derived targets measure training fit, even when absent from their input prefixes.

Popularity matching and text-similar distractors lack precise definitions and fallback rules. Text similarity alone does not establish an adjacent-interest mismatch; candidate popularity and metadata coverage can confound comparisons.

The report does not specify diagnostic runtime limits or a controlled experiment connecting diagnostics to validation gains. Difficulty 3 appears optimistic given architecture adaptation and deterministic sampling; future potential 8 remains speculative.

follow_up_queries.reason: Resolve feature alignment and distinguish training memorization from useful ranking discrimination before implementing the adapter.
follow_up_queries.query: In SASRec next-item recommendation diagnostics using training-derived prefix/target pairs, how should left padding, sequence truncation, repeated targets, final-position feature extraction, and candidate scoring shapes be handled? What sanity checks detect target leakage and distinguish training-fit ranks from generalization without changing the existing validation split?

follow_up_queries.reason: Make the three challenge distributions reproducible and identify shortcuts that could explain rank differences.
follow_up_queries.query: For sequential recommendation diagnostics comparing uniform training-sampler, popularity-matched, and TF-IDF title/description-similar distractors, how should popularity bins, similarity reference items, unique candidate sampling, exclusions, missing-text fallbacks, and deterministic ties be specified? What controls separate semantic difficulty from popularity and metadata-coverage effects when distractor relevance is unknown?

follow_up_queries.reason: Determine whether the diagnostic justifies its cost and whether a simpler alternative offers more actionable evidence.
follow_up_queries.query: Under a fixed 43,200 GPU-second recommendation search budget, how can a small prespecified ablation compare frozen training-rank diagnostics with controlled history-deletion probes and simple popularity or recency baselines? How should paired per-user validation HR@10 changes across four datasets be analyzed while accounting for adaptive model selection and training-seed uncertainty?
